name: Old Maid
description: Old Maid is a timeless children's card game focused on matching and evasion. Using a standard deck with one card removed (or a specialized deck), players aim to pair up all their cards and discard them. The tension lies in the final unmatchable card—the 'Old Maid'. The player left with this card at the end of the game loses. It is a game of simple mechanics, bluffing, and luck.

history.origins: Dates back to the early 19th century. It likely evolved from older gambling games where the loser had to pay for drinks ('Black Peter' in Germany, 'Le Pouilleux' in France).
timeline: 1830s: First literary mentions of Old Maid as a nursery game.
1880s: Milton Bradley and Parker Brothers begin manufacturing dedicated Old Maid decks with comical characters.
1950s: Becomes one of the 'Big Four' children's card games (alongside Go Fish, Crazy Eights, and Slapjack).
Present: A universal introductory game for teaching youngsters card handling and turn-taking.
history.cultural: Known by many regional names: Black Peter (Germany), Musta Pekka (Finland), and Scabby Queen (UK).
history.evolution: The game was originally used as a semi-gambling game for adults but shifted toward a purely social/family game by the late Victorian era.

setup.deck: Standard cards. Remove the Queen of Clubs. The Queen of Spades becomes the 'Old Maid'.
setup.dealing: Deal all cards out one by one. It doesn't matter if some players have one more card than others.
setup.equipment: Standard 52-card pack with one Queen removed, or a dedicated Old Maid deck.

rules.objective: Pair up and discard all your cards; the player left holding the single remaining Queen (the Old Maid) at the end loses.
rules.gameplay: The dealer deals all 51 cards one by one; some players may have one more card. Everyone discards any pairs (and from triplets or quartets, discard two or two pairs). The dealer offers their hand face down to the player on their left, who draws one card without looking. If it makes a pair they discard the pair. The player who drew then offers their hand to the next player left; play continues clockwise. Players drop out when their hand is empty. The player left holding the single Queen (the Old Maid) loses.
keyRules: Pairs are two cards of equal rank (e.g. two sevens or two kings).
The player who just drew a card offers their hand to the next player to their left.
If you empty your hand you are safe and take no further part; turn passes to the next player.
The holder of the single remaining Queen (Old Maid) at the end loses.

strategy.basic: Keep your cards spread out! If you are holding the Old Maid, try to keep your face neutral. If the player drawing from you sees you smiling or looking nervous when they touch a certain card, they will avoid it. Conversely, if you want them to pick it, try to hide it slightly higher or lower in your hand so it 'sticks out' naturally.
strategy.intermediate: The 'Card Shuffle': When it's your turn to have a card drawn, shuffle your hand behind your back or under the table. This prevents the drawing player from tracking where you moved the Old Maid from the previous round.
strategy.advanced: Bluff-Targeting: If you have two cards and one is the Old Maid, you can try to trick the opponent by holding the 'safe' card slightly forward. Many children reflexively pick the 'easiest' card to grab. If you know an opponent uses this habit, place the Old Maid in the prominent position.
tips: In a specialized deck, the Old Maid often has a distinct character (the 'Nanny' or 'Aunt'). Children often focus on the art, which makes bluffing harder!
If you draw a card that completes a pair, discard it IMMEDIATELY to reduce your hand size and improve your odds of not having the Old Maid drawn back from you.

variations.name: Black Peter
variations.description: A Jack is removed instead of a Queen; the holder of the odd Jack at the end loses. Often played with a special 31- or 37-card pack where the odd card depicts a black cat or chimney sweep.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses same engine; only deck and odd card differ; no numeric overrides needed.

variations.name: Reversed Old Maid
variations.description: Same mechanics but the holder of the odd card (last Queen or Old Maid) at the end is the winner instead of the loser.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant only inverts win condition; engine logic unchanged; no overrides needed.

variations.name: Dedicated Old Maid Pack
variations.description: Special pack of matching pairs plus one Old Maid card (e.g. comical character); the single Old Maid card has no pair and its holder loses.
variations.emptyOverridesReason: Variant uses dedicated deck; same phases and actions; no engine overrides needed.

scoring.description: Avoid being the player left with the Old Maid. Cards in hand count as penalty; first to zero cards wins.
scoring.winCondition: Avoid being the player left with the Old Maid.
